narrative.overview: lelam's visual language pairs a warm, paper-like marketplace with the clarity of an editorial ledger. Real product photography carries the emotional weight; serif headlines and restrained olive accents give the interface its recognizable voice. White cards sit quietly on cream, divided by fine rules rather than heavy panels. The seller surfaces extend the same world: a fanned deck and handwritten notes on the sell landing, then compact, scannable ledgers for daily operations.
keyCharacteristics: Cream, ink, olive, and hairline borders.
DM Serif Display headlines; DM Sans controls and body; Caveat for brief handwritten notes.
Real product imagery, pill controls, and calm editorial spacing.

rules.name: The One Olive Rule
rules.body: Use olive as a focused guide, not as a full-screen wash.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Serif for story and hierarchy; sans for operation. Handwriting is decorative, never the only carrier of meaning.

dos: Do keep the paper/ink/olive palette and DM Serif Display + DM Sans pairing.
Do use product photography as the primary visual material.
Do keep seller text at 12px or larger and controls easy to tap.
Do let borders, spacing, and type hierarchy do most of the organizing.
donts: Don't add a new accent palette or replace the editorial type pairing without a deliberate brand change.
Don't rely on tiny metadata, decorative handwriting, or color alone to communicate a task state.
Don't turn the seller dashboard into a generic dense grid of dark panels.
